alerts.subject: Christmas Eve Luminarias: NM Women's Chorus, Scout Troops 395/1395 & AYS Now Selling
alerts.body:
Hello Neighbors,

We recently received information that the NM Women's Chorus will be selling luminarias that include delivery, set-up, and pickup. For those of you wishing for this full service, please see the link below.

NM Women's Chorus: https://www.nmwomenschorus.org/

As HCNA receives information about which groups are selling luminarias this year, we want to make sure we share them with all of you. Below are two groups selling luminarias this year. These groups are only selling and delivering luminarias. They do not set up or pick up.

• Scout Troops 395 and 1395 (selling and delivering only; no set-up or pickup): https://scoutsluminarias.com/shop-1

• Albuquerque Youth Symphony Program (selling and delivering only; no set-up or pickup): https://www.aysmusic.org

Many of us have relied on Boy Scout Troop 444 for luminaria purchase, setup, and removal. The Troop will no longer be offering this service. Their message is below.

— Message from Troop 444 —

Troop 444 has provided Christmas Eve luminarias to the Albuquerque Country Club neighborhood for over 30 years, but this year, that tradition is coming to an end. Troop 444 will no longer be offering our annual Christmas luminaria service.

We sincerely thank everyone who supported the Troop over the years. Your orders helped generations of Scouts pay for activities, equipment, camping, and other experiences that made Scouting possible.

Many of you supported this fundraiser year after year, and we are especially grateful for that loyalty. It has been a pleasure to be part of the neighborhood's Christmas Eve tradition. Thank you for supporting Troop 444 and its Scouts for more than three decades.

— Troop 444

alerts.subject: Neighborhood Habitat Walk — Nov 11
alerts.body:
Get to know your wild neighbors! Join us on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, from 2:00 to 4:00 PM for a walk starting at Aldo and Estella Leopold's historic home. We'll explore the neighborhood habitat and talk about ways to share space with our wild neighbors. We'll also make observations with the iNaturalist app to add to our urban biodiversity map!

Where: Aldo Leopold House, 135 14th Street SW (one block south of Central Avenue)

Tip: Download the free iNaturalist app before the walk.

Map: Aldo Leopold House — https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=135+14th+Street+SW+Albuquerque+NM+87102

Get the iNaturalist app — https://www.inaturalist.org

alerts.subject: Barbara Garcia Memorial Fund Drive for Roadrunner Food Bank
alerts.body:
Dear Neighbors,

Please see the message below from Rudy Garcia, HCNA Board President.

Thanks,

HCNA

Dear Neighbors,

In 2019, Barbara Garcia, my wife and your fellow neighbor started a neighborhood food drive for Roadrunner Food Bank. Barbara was very concerned about food insecurity and wanted to ensure that Albuquerque families would not go hungry. She asked the HCNA board for approval to sponsor the drive in the neighborhood. The neighborhood provided 926 lbs. of food. This first drive was a success.

In 2020, she asked the board for approval to do another food drive and developed an online drive to include the surrounding downtown neighborhoods who wanted to participate. This continued through 2025 with more neighborhoods participating. In 2025, HCNA and the surrounding downtown neighborhoods raised $16,000 which provided 80,000 meals for families in need. Every $1 helps provide up to five meals.

Sadly, Barbara passed away a few weeks ago. Before she passed, she asked me to please continue the online food drive and I promised I would. I asked the board for approval and they unanimously approved it. Because of her efforts, the Roadrunner Food Bank this year renamed the drive the Barbara Garcia Memorial Fund Drive.

Hungry New Mexicans need our help due to the high price of food along with cuts in federal funding. According to Roadrunner Food Bank, “the need is especially great this year while high living costs and threats to accessible services are pushing more families into food insecurity.”

Our goal this year is $20,000! We hope that you will contribute generously but any amount is extremely helpful and appreciated. Donations can be made anonymously, and some companies will match donations. Below is the link to donate:

https://give.rrfb.org/feedingourneighbors

For additional information on food insecurity please click on the link below from Downtown Albuquerque News.

https://us3.campaign-archive.com/?u=306fc3b21030d6f0128cc4af9&id=410d8f9084

In honor of Barbara Garcia, we and Roadrunner Food Bank thank you in advance for your support!

Sincerely,

Rudy Garcia

President

HCNA Board

rmgconsults@msn.com
